title: Concurrent Multi-Priority Adaptive Scheduling Validation

method.edge_load: Two bounded CPU busy-loop workers on Edge EC2, approximately 50 seconds
method.edge_cloud_resource_metrics: Fetched from live Edge and Cloud /metrics endpoints while Edge was under pressure
method.network_latency: Controlled request input, 80 ms usable and 250 ms constrained; not an injected physical network impairment
method.concurrency: 6 simultaneous scheduler API requests per batch
method.workload_ids: Stable independent workload ID per priority

policy_behavior.usable_network_and_edge_overloaded: All priorities offloaded to healthy Cloud
policy_behavior.constrained_network_and_edge_overloaded: Low and Medium queued; High retained on Edge best-effort

limitations: Only scheduler decisions were exercised concurrently; this milestone does not claim 18 simultaneous inference executions.
Network latency values of 80 ms and 250 ms were controlled scheduler inputs. Edge and Cloud resource metrics were live.
High priority is best-effort pinned to Edge when Edge is overloaded and Cloud offload is not viable; this does not guarantee a latency SLO.
Single scheduler replica; state is in-memory and process-local.
